title: Porchetta
subtitle: Italian herb-stuffed rolled pork
excerpt: A whole pork belly rolled with garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds, and black pepper, then slow-roasted until the outside is deeply crackling and the meat is juicy and perfumed with herbs.

recipe.sourceNotes: Porchetta is a traditional Italian roast pork preparation from Central Italy, particularly associated with Lazio, Umbria, and Sardinia. It is sold from street stalls throughout Italy and is one of the dishes most associated with Italian sagre (food festivals).

recipeTools.notes: A large roasting tin to catch the fat.

content.text: Porchetta is a pork belly laid flat, covered in a paste of garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds, and black pepper, then rolled tightly and roasted slowly until the outside is deeply golden and crackling and the meat inside is soft and fragrant with herbs. It slices into rings that show the swirl of the filling.

items.preparation: boned and butterflied, skin scored at 1 cm intervals

content.text: Pound or blend the garlic, rosemary leaves, fennel seeds, black pepper, 1 teaspoon of the salt, and olive oil together into a coarse paste. Stir in the lemon zest.
Lay the pork belly skin-side down. Spread the herb paste over the flesh side. Roll up tightly from the long edge. Tie at 3 cm intervals with kitchen twine to hold the roll.

Rub the remaining salt over the skin and into the score lines. Place on a wire rack in a roasting tin, skin-side up. Refrigerate uncovered overnight so the skin dries out completely. This is key for good crackling.
Take the pork out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking. Heat the oven to 230 C / fan 210 C / gas 8. Roast for 30 minutes to start crisping the skin.
Reduce the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3 and continue roasting for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, until an instant-read thermometer in the centre reads 70 C.
If the crackling is not fully crisp, return to 230 C for a final 10 minutes. Rest for 20 minutes before removing the twine and slicing.
